extracted.subtask_description: Ethical guidance for mobile reporters on responsible reporting practices, including fairness, editorial independence, accountability, and maintaining audience trust when producing news using mobile tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on an issue, especially if it implicates a certain individual or group, it’s important to reach out and give that party a chance to respond and give their statement and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively contact implicated parties to obtain their response and perspective; ensure reporting presents opportunities for affected individuals/groups to comment rather than presenting only one side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: While accepting a scholarship, grant or fellowship to report on a story is not against journalism ethics, you should not be sponsored by a political group, corporation or individual to tell a particular story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting funding for reporting (scholarships, grants, fellowships) can be permissible, but avoid direct sponsorships or agreements with political groups, corporations, or individuals that would dictate story content or bias coverage; disclose relevant funding where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: You should make sure that all of the information you provide is accurate to the best of your knowledge and be able to testify to this in court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify facts before publishing, keep records/sources that support reporting, correct errors promptly, and be prepared to substantiate claims legally if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain audience trust / truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Know that your audience trusts you to be a source of truthful information. Breaking that trust doesn’t just reflect on you; it can cause your audience to be less trustful of journalists as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize truthful, factual reporting to preserve and restore public confidence in the media; recognize that individual breaches of trust have wider consequences for public trust in journalism, especially when overall trust is low.
